description.description_long: CNN’s July 31, 2015 account reported that Trump used S&A Concrete to build Trump Plaza condominiums and cited federal court records identifying Anthony Salerno and Paul Castellano as controllers of S&A. A Second Circuit opinion in a federal concrete-industry case described a jury forfeiture verdict awarding the government Salerno’s interest in S&A Concrete and affiliates from November 1981 through the end of 1984. The same opinion reversed all appealing defendants’ convictions and remanded for further proceedings. It does not mention Trump or Trump Plaza. Together, these sources support an attributed account of the reported supplier relationship and Salerno’s interest in the company; they do not establish that Trump knew of or joined a criminal scheme, violated RICO, or that the Trump Plaza project benefited from criminal conduct. This correction removes the frozen original’s unsupported land-price and concrete-cost figures and its conclusions of criminal participation while preserving the same reported Trump Plaza supplier event.
description.description_medium: CNN reported that Trump used S&A Concrete to build Trump Plaza condominiums and cited records identifying Anthony Salerno and Paul Castellano as controllers. In a related concrete-industry case, the Second Circuit recorded a jury forfeiture verdict involving Salerno’s interest in S&A, then reversed all appealing defendants’ convictions and remanded. The opinion does not mention Trump. This supports an attributed supplier relationship, not knowing participation or a RICO violation.

pinned_prior_correction.description_medium: Two linked reports describe Trump’s historical business dealings with firms and people alleged to have organized-crime ties. CNN recounts property and construction claims based on journalists, books, state records and federal records, and notes Trump was questioned in investigations that led to no criminal charges. This material documents attributed allegations and scrutiny; it does not establish that he joined a racketeering enterprise or violated RICO.
pinned_prior_correction.description_long: CNN’s report collects allegations about Trump’s business dealings with organized-crime figures and companies in New York and Atlantic City. It recounts that Trump paid $1.1 million for an Atlantic City parcel in 1982 after Salvatore Testa and a partner reportedly bought it for $195,000 in 1977. The article says two construction firms controlled by Philadelphia mob figures helped build the casino, citing a New Jersey state commission report, and describes Trump’s use of the mob-controlled S&A concrete company for Trump Plaza condos and Trump Tower, based on federal records discussed by journalist Wayne Barrett. CNN also notes Trump was a target of a 1979 bribery investigation and questioned in a 1981 racketeering probe; the cited investigations did not result in criminal charges. The reporting documents attributed claims about contacts and business relationships. It does not establish that Trump knowingly joined a criminal enterprise, violated RICO, or participated in a racketeering conspiracy. Those conclusions require primary records and evidence beyond the linked articles.
